record.paper_title: Some open problems of Ramsey minimal graphs.
record.context_brief: Ramsey-minimal graphs versus two disjoint paths
record.original_question: Let F, G, and H be non-empty graphs, and write F → (G, H) to mean that every red-blue coloring of the edges of F contains either a red copy of G or a blue copy of H. A graph F is Ramsey (G, H)-minimal if F → (G, H) but, for every edge e of F, the graph F − e fails to satisfy F − e → (G, H). Let ℜ(G, H) denote the set of all Ramsey (G, H)-minimal graphs. For each integer n ≥ 4, classify all graphs in ℜ(2K2, 2Pn), where 2K2 is the matching consisting of two disjoint edges and 2Pn denotes the disjoint union of two copies of the path graph on n vertices.

evidence.quote: F, G, and H, say that F → (G, H) if whenever the edges of F are 2-colored, say with red and blue, there is either a red copy of G or a blue copy of H. A graph F is called Ramsey (G, H)-minimal if F → (G, H) but for any edge e ∈ E(F), we have (F - e) ↛ (G, H). The set of all Ramsey (G, H)-minimal graphs, the topic of this note, is denoted by ℜ(G, H).
For each n ≥ 4, characterize the graphs in ℜ(2K2, 2Pn).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let F, G, H be non-empty simple graphs. Write F → (G, H) to mean that for every red–blue coloring of the edges of F, either there is a subgraph of F isomorphic to G all of whose edges are red, or there is a subgraph of F isomorphic to H all of whose edges are blue. A graph F is called Ramsey (G, H)-minimal if F → (G, H) and, for every edge e of F, the graph F − e does not satisfy F − e → (G, H). Let ℜ(G, H) denote the class (up to isomorphism) of all Ramsey (G, H)-minimal graphs.

Let 2K₂ denote the graph consisting of two vertex-disjoint edges, let Pₙ denote the path on n vertices, and let 2Pₙ denote the disjoint union of two copies of Pₙ.

Problem. For each integer n ≥ 4, give a complete classification (up to isomorphism) of all graphs in ℜ(2K₂, 2Pₙ).
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: Tatanto and Baskoro (AIP Conf. Proc. 1450, 2012) gave necessary conditions for members of ℜ(2K₂, 2Pₙ) for n ≥ 3, showed that the only disconnected members arise as 3Pₙ or as F ∪ G with F, G connected members of ℜ(2K₂, Pₙ), and completely characterized ℜ(2K₂, 2P₃). A full classification for n ≥ 4 has not been reported and the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: On Ramsey (2K2, 2Pn)-minimal graphs (Tatanto–Baskoro)
status_evidence.snippet: They give necessary conditions for the members of R(2K2, 2Pn) for n ≥ 3 and determine all graphs in R(2K2, 2P3).
status_evidence.claim: Only partial characterization (n=3 and structural conditions) is established; n ≥ 4 case is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Problems of Ramsey Minimal Graphs (SpringerLink)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists characterization of ℜ(2K₂, 2Pₙ) for n ≥ 4 as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The classification problem for n ≥ 4 is posed as open.
